newsitem.title: USA: G24 worried by 10-year low in official aid levels.
newsitem.headline: G24 worried by 10-year low in official aid levels.

text.p: Developing countries say private capital cannot replace the flow of aid from rich donor states and international organizations, which has fallen to a 10-year low.
A draft communique of the Group of 24 developing countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America, said official development assistance (ODA) had fallen to its lowest level in 10 years.
The communique, to be released on Sunday after a meeting of G24 ministers during International Monetary Fund/World Bank talks in Washington, was obtained by Reuters on Saturday.
"Deputies ... emphasized that private capital flows are no substitute for official flows for alleviating poverty in (the poorest) and other developing countries," the communique said.
"The absence of adequate ODA funds would adversely affect the growth potential of recipient countries and ... exacerbate migratory pressures on countries with better prospects."
The G24 said they recognized the benefits of liberalizing capital transactions, but said countries should be allowed to "reimpose restrictions under specific circumstances".
A sustainable macroeconomic climate, well capitalized banks and a clear legal system had to be in place to ensure that capital transactions could be liberalized successfully.
